messages.author: 4d4056ff666dae36
messages.subject: Multinomial distribution
parts:
Hello everybody,

I am David and I am a new user of Stan and I want to implement a hierarchical model with multinomial distribution but I have the following error:

"""
No matches for: 

  int ~ multinomial(vector)

Available argument signatures for multinomial:

  int[] ~ multinomial(vector)

require real scalar return type for probability function.

"""
Please help me because I don´t understand what is the problem here.


Thanks 
David

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Multinomial distribution
parts:
It helps if you send us your program, not just fragments
of output.

> On Mar 12, 2017, at 1:23 PM, David Vivas <vivad...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Hello everybody,
>
> I am David and I am a new user of Stan and I want to implement a hierarchical model with multinomial distribution but I have the following error:
>
> """
> No matches for:
>
> int ~ multinomial(vector)

Somewhere you are using

a ~ multinomial(theta)

where a is an integer.

> Available argument signatures for multinomial:
>
> int[] ~ multinomial(vector)

You need to write

b ~ multinomial(theta)

where b is an array of integers. These are counts for
each outcome.

- Bob

Thanks again Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Multinomial distribution
parts:
You might want to scan through the manual to see how to program
various things in Stan.

transformed data {
int b[3] = { 5093, 1493, 2190 };

if you just have constants. Typically, you declare b as data:

data {
int b[3];

and read it in from the outside.

- Bob
